title: ERCOT Sees Surge in Power Demand by 2030s Amid Data Center Growth
source_used: San Antonio Express-News (16 Apr 2026) and Houston Public Media (22 Apr 2026) on the same ERCOT forecast
key_facts: ERCOT, the Texas grid operator, forecast in its long-term load forecast that peak demand could more than quadruple by 2032, boosted by data centers and other large users, population growth and severe weather.
This summer's peak was projected at 98,000 MW, up from the 85,508 MW record of Aug. 10, 2023; by 2029 demand was projected at 278,003 MW and by 2032 at 376,790 MW.
Most growth comes from large loads such as data centers, crypto miners and industrial users; data centers were projected at about 65% of large-load demand this year.

Houston Public Media: ERCOT and the Public Utility Commission of Texas chair said the long-term figure is likely an overestimate because it relies on utility responses about proposed projects; ERCOT is looking to revise it.
PowerHouse Texas's executive director called the number a high-end planning scenario, 'not a firm prediction'.
quote_evidence: Electricity usage in Texas is expected to smash records this summer as the state grid operator braces for peak demand to more than quadruple by 2032, boosted by data centers and other big users flocking to the state, population growth and increasingly severe weather.
As a result, its forecast is likely an overestimate, grid operators told the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) late last week.

why_it_matters_hint: Texas is planning for huge data-center load, but ERCOT itself says the long-range number is probably too high.
